llm_system_prompt: You brainstorm what an image dynamic could stand for. Output ONLY strict JSON — no commentary, no markdown fences.
llm_user_prompt:
Plain visual read of the image:
${step1Output}

The image's physical analog (core = the binding relational skeleton; secondary = nice-to-have texture):
${step2Output}

The ensemble + secondary entities:
${step3Output}

What type of situation might you use this as a metaphor for (list 2-5 distinct situations)? DISTINCT means different domains — not rewordings of the same idea.

TYPES, not instances: each item is an abstract PATTERN that many concrete stories could fill — not one specific scene with particular people. THE TEST: could you name 3+ unrelated concrete examples that all fit the item? If the item names specific actors or props (a cashier, a couple, an omelet), it is an instance — generalize it.
WRONG: "a customer explaining a questionable return while the cashier silently doubts the story" — one concrete scene
RIGHT: "ignoring an obvious problem while carrying on as normal" — a pattern countless scenes could fill

BRAINSTORM FREELY: straight from what the image FEELS like — lived situations a person would recognize and post about, in plain human words; vivid beats systematic. WRONG register: "a rigorous technical system depending on one bizarre legacy component" — a spec, not a feeling. RIGHT register: "having to treat the team's one ridiculous member as completely normal". (Register illustrations only — NEVER copy either into output; derive your situations from THIS image.)

STAGE THE CORE: every situation must restage the analog's CORE relationship — the core is binding; the plain read and secondary texture are only flavor. THE CAST TEST (run on every situation): fill each core slot from the situation and check that each entity keeps its ATTITUDE and its RELATIONSHIP to the others. If any slot-filler's attitude flips (entities the core shows on the same side become skeptics, judges, rivals, or reluctant participants), the situation FAILS — discard it, do not soften it.
WRONG: for a core of one enthusiastic entity among same-kind teammates united and ready to act — "the optimistic new hire meeting the seasoned veterans who know how things really work" (the united teammates are recast as jaded gatekeepers; their unity and readiness are gone)
RIGHT: "being the one member of the team who's visibly hyped for the mission while the rest keep a straight game face" (every core entity keeps its attitude; the group stays one team)
(Illustrations only — never copy them into output; derive your situations from THIS image's core.)

RATE each situation twice, 0-1, scored honestly and independently (a resonant situation can still be invisible in the image, and vice versa):
- resonance — THE TEST: would a real person see their own life in this and post it? 1.0 = a "this is literally me" common experience; 0.3 = recognizable but niche or bloodless.
- image_clarity — THE TEST: could a viewer name this relationship/dynamic from the image ALONE, no caption? 1.0 = the picture shows it outright; 0.3 = only the caption would reveal it.
WRONG: every situation scored 0.8-0.9 on both — the ratings must separate the list, not decorate it
RIGHT: a universally felt situation the image only hints at → resonance 0.9, image_clarity 0.4

ANTI-FAILURE CHECKLIST (verify before output):
• a situation whose core_cast drops a core entity or flips its attitude → FAIL, discard the situation
• a situation that pits core entities against each other when the core shows them on the same side → FAIL, discard it
• a core_cast you can only write by changing an attitude → FAIL, discard it

Output ONLY a JSON array of 2-5 objects: [{"situation": "<the pattern, plain human words>", "core_cast": "<one sentence: who fills each core slot in this situation, each keeping its attitude and side>", "resonance": <0-1>, "resonance_why": "<one short reason>", "image_clarity": <0-1>, "clarity_why": "<one short reason>"}]
